clue.text: Number of characters in Romeo and Juliet older than Juliet? Just so

definitions.text: Number of characters in Romeo and Juliet
definitions.meaning: count the letters in the title: ROMEO (5), AND (3), JULIET (6)
Juliet is thirteen in the play, a fortnight short of her next birthday, so the age just above hers

explanation.surface: A trivia question about the cast of Shakespeare's play and which characters are older than the heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' looks like people in the play, but it means letters in the title. Juliet's Nurse says she is not yet fourteen, so 'just' older than her is that age.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings land on the same number: the letter count of the title and the age just above thirteen.

clue.text: Outlaw said in France to be gang member

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it
dit is French for 'said'

explanation.surface: A French outlaw is reported to be part of a criminal gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' reads as the definition (a noun), but it is the verb, giving BAN; the definition is at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber who typically operates as one of an armed band.

clue.text: Part of scale that is least likely to collapse

parts.note: sol (soh) is the fifth note of the tonic sol-fa scale
id est is Latin for 'that is', abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: Of the parts of a weighing scale, one is the sturdiest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scale' suggests weighing apparatus, but it is the musical scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Something most firm and robust in construction is the least prone to fall down.

clue.text: A large group of hunters ending off a domesticated mammal

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: the final letter of the hunting group's word is removed

parts.note: a pack is a group of wolves or hounds that hunt together

explanation.surface: A big pack of hunters stops chasing a farm animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American camelid kept by people for its wool, a domestic relative of the llama.

clue.text: They may draw diners in and earn some cash, totally without tips

indicators.note: every one of the three words loses its first and last letter, its tips, leaving only the insides

explanation.surface: Restaurant staff are told how to lure customers and make money, with no tips at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tips' suggests gratuities to waiters; here it is the ends of the words. EARN, SOME and CASH lose their tips to leave AR, OM and AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Appetising smells wafting from a kitchen are what tempt passers-by into a restaurant.

clue.text: Cooling system in a vehicle that's helpful for summer?

indicators.note: the cooling system goes inside the vehicle's word

parts.note: a bus is a road vehicle
AC is short for air conditioning

explanation.surface: Air conditioning in a car would be welcome in hot summer weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' is not the season but one who sums, so the definition is a frame for counting beads.
explanation.definitionFit: A bead frame is a calculating aid, so it helps a person doing arithmetic.

clue.text: Less than striking action in game's nadir

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game, and go is also a board game; with the 's attached
the nadir is the lowest point, a low

explanation.surface: A dull moment in a match lacks any striking action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less than striking' sounds like 'unimpressive', but it means short of a full strike: industrial action where workers deliberately slow down.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliberate slowdown at work is a protest falling short of an outright walkout.

clue.text: Apply bleach when covering it

indicators.note: the word when wraps around the word it

explanation.surface: An instruction to use bleach once something has been covered.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleaching a fabric or surface makes it paler, which is the verb's meaning.

clue.text: Almost fight over articles about cold fatty snack

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over the rest
the word for a fight is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a scrap is a fight

indicators.note: the word for articles goes around the cold letter

parts.note: articles are things, items
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A near brawl over things breaks out about something cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' works because this is a down clue, so the first piece sits on top. Pork scratchings are crisp fried pieces of pork rind sold in British pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pork scratchings are crunchy morsels of fried pig skin and fat, a bar snack.

clue.text: Holy, as reflected by almost all doctrine

indicators.note: a mirror image reads the word backwards
the word for doctrine loses its last letter

parts.note: a credo is a creed, a statement of doctrine

explanation.surface: Holiness is mirrored in nearly every religious teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sacred is consecrated and venerated, set apart as holy.

clue.text: Relating to the elements, reaching exciting conclusions once carbon's extracted

indicators.note: the carbon letter is pulled out of the longer word

parts.note: climactic means forming a climax, the exciting high point at the end
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A chemistry write-up on elements reaches thrilling findings once carbon is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The elements' suggests chemistry, but it means the weather. 'once ... extracted' takes a C out of CLIMACTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The elements are wind, rain and weather; climatic concerns climate.

clue.text: Draw, as rule, after switching sides

indicators.note: sides are right and left, R and L, which trade places in the word rule

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Drawing a line with a ruler after changing which side you work from.
explanation.walkthrough: R (right) and L (left) swap places in RULE.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw someone in is to attract or entice them, as bait tempts a fish.

clue.text: Mastered an amended part of commercial vocabulary

indicators.note: amended means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has learned a corrected section of business jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: Brand titles such as product labels are words registered and used in commerce.

clue.text: Centres of population, as found in the rest of the across answers

definitions.meaning: the crowded central districts of large towns

definitions.text: as found in the rest of the across answers
definitions.meaning: every other across answer has a city inside it: ROMA, OSLO, ACRE, LIMA, UR, ADEN, BERLIN, LA, TURIN, ULM, RIO, NY

explanation.surface: The puzzle's theme clue announces where the urban centres are concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: towns sit inside the other across lights, such as BERLIN in TIMBERLINE and OSLO in GOSLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban cores are the densely populated middle parts of big towns.

clue.text: Rise late, perhaps — or before all the others

indicators.note: perhaps flags that these letters are one possible arrangement of others

explanation.surface: Get up late, or else be the very first up.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface contrasts rising late with rising early; 'perhaps' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming first in time, ahead of everyone else, means being soonest of all.

clue.text: Allowing to get licence, finally, and catch fish

indicators.note: only the closing letter of licence is taken

parts.note: to nab is to catch or seize
the ling is a long food fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An angler gets a permit and then catches a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Permitting something to happen is making it possible, giving the means.

clue.text: Producer of drone group of spies used to trap villain

indicators.note: the spy agency's letters close round the villain

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
a cad is a rotter, an ungentlemanly villain

explanation.surface: Intelligence agents deploy a drone to catch a wrongdoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drone' suggests a spy aircraft; here it is a continuous buzzing noise.
explanation.definitionFit: This insect makes a loud, monotonous droning sound with its body.

clue.text: It spells end of vegetation, when put on a tree

definitions.text: It spells end of vegetation, when put on a tree

indicators.note: in a down clue the single letter is placed on top of the rest
only the closing letter of vegetation is taken

parts.note: the palm is a tree

explanation.surface: A defoliant dropped on a tree means the end of plant life.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: napalm destroys vegetation, and the wordplay is N (end of vegetation) on A PALM.
explanation.definitionFit: This jellied incendiary was used in war to burn away forest cover.

clue.text: Equivalent of money, including capital, that is at the upper limit of growth

indicators.note: the word for the money equivalent holds the capital inside

parts.note: from the saying 'time is money'
Berlin is the capital of Germany

explanation.surface: A financial note about money and capital reaching a ceiling of growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Money' and 'capital' look like a finance theme, but capital is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: On mountains, trees stop growing above a certain altitude, the tree line.

clue.text: Virus that is pierced by old medical instrument

indicators.note: the old letter goes into the combined pieces

parts.note: a bug is an informal word for a virus or infection
i.e. abbreviates Latin id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: An infection is caused by an antique medical device puncturing the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A bougie is a thin flexible rod a doctor inserts to widen or examine a body passage.

clue.text: Initially formed euphemism from guy mostly concealing name

indicators.note: the shortened word hides the name letter inside it
the word for guy loses its final letter

parts.note: a guy is an effigy of Guy Fawkes burned on Bonfire Night in Britain

explanation.surface: A polite term made up from a straw dummy hiding its name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially formed' is the definition's own joke: the euphemism is built from the initial F of a swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: The mild substitute stands in for a stronger expletive and is made from its first letter.

clue.text: Letters regularly falling out of mailbags, unfortunately

indicators.note: every other letter is shaken out of the word, as letters spill from a sack

explanation.surface: Post keeps tumbling out of the mail sacks, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters are the alphabet kind: m-A-i-L-b-A-g-S gives the second, fourth, sixth and eighth.
explanation.definitionFit: This interjection expresses regret or sorrow, much like 'sadly'.

clue.text: Starting to create family in which you are reportedly growing up

indicators.note: the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: mating is pairing up to breed, starting a family

indicators.note: signals that the words are rendered as they are heard

parts.note: the two words spoken quickly give the letters U and R, as in text speak

explanation.surface: Starting a family is the stage in which you are said to grow up.
explanation.definitionFit: Developing towards adulthood or ripeness is to come of age.

clue.text: Seabird needed by grateful mariner

indicators.note: needed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A thankful sailor relies on a bird at sea, perhaps echoing the Ancient Mariner's albatross.
explanation.definitionFit: The fulmar is a grey and white petrel of northern oceans.

clue.text: Vocal performance in opera included by impresario sometimes

indicators.note: the answer is held within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An opera producer occasionally slips in a singing turn of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: An arioso is a melodic passage between recitative and aria, sung in opera.

clue.text: Soon switched my name, such as Brendan

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon, shortly

indicators.note: the two letters of my change round

explanation.surface: The setter says they will shortly change their name.
explanation.walkthrough: Brendan is this puzzle's setter, writing under a pseudonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A false or assumed name hides a writer's real identity, as crossword setters' pen names do.
